items.title: Where Each Immeasurable Reaches Its Height, and Why Only the Noble Truly Cultivate Them

items.zh: 憶念空處修習悲心，亦最第一。以修悲者樂欲拔苦，無色界中遠離眾苦，斷壞等苦彼都無故。是故憶念無邊空處修悲等至，作如是念：當令一切有苦有情，到無眾苦及所依處。修喜定者，亦常憶念無邊識處，慶諸有情所得安樂。作如是念：當令一切有情之類受無量樂，猶如識處，識無限量。是故憶念識無邊處修習喜定，為最第一。
items.en: Recalling the space-sphere and cultivating compassion is likewise supreme. Because one who cultivates compassion wishes to remove suffering, and in the formless realm the manifold sufferings are left behind — the sufferings of breaking and injury and the rest being wholly absent there. Therefore, recalling the sphere of infinite space, one cultivates the compassion-attainment, thinking: "may all suffering beings reach freedom from every suffering, and the abode that supports it." One who cultivates the joy-concentration likewise constantly recalls the sphere of infinite consciousness, rejoicing in the ease beings attain, thinking: "may all beings receive measureless happiness, like consciousness itself, without limit." Therefore recalling the sphere of infinite consciousness and cultivating the joy-concentration is supreme.

items.zh: 修捨定者，亦常憶念無所有處。作如是念：無所有處，無漏心地最為後邊，捨最第一；如阿羅漢苾芻，一切苦、樂、不苦不樂現行位中，皆無染污。當令一切有情之類，得如是捨。是故憶念無所有處修習捨定，為最第一。如是一切皆是聖行，唯聖能修，故經宣說覺分俱行。
items.en: One who cultivates the equanimity-concentration likewise constantly recalls the sphere of nothingness, thinking: "the sphere of nothingness is the very last ground of the uncontaminated mind, where equanimity is supreme — as an arhat monk, in every occurrence of pain, pleasure, or the neither, is without defilement; may all beings attain such equanimity." Therefore recalling the sphere of nothingness and cultivating the equanimity-concentration is supreme. All these are noble practice, cultivable only by the noble; therefore the sūtra proclaims [them] as cultivated together with the awakening-factors.

items.title: One-Part and Complete Cultivation, and the Eleven Difficulties of the Light-Concentration

items.zh: 復次，云何一分修三摩地？謂於此中，或唯作意思光明相，或唯作意思惟色相，而入於定。如是二種，隨其次第，或了光明，或覩眾色。云何具分修三摩地？謂俱思惟而入於定，亦了光明，亦見眾色。
items.en: Furthermore, what is one-part cultivation of concentration? Here, either attending only to the mark of light or attending only to the mark of form, one enters the concentration; these two, in order, either discern light or behold forms. What is complete-cultivation of concentration? Attending to both, one enters the concentration, discerning light and also seeing forms.

items.zh: 如是修習光明定者，定難差別有十一種。所謂疑等，如經廣說。問：此誰難耶？答：三摩地相。相有二種。謂所緣相及因緣相。用彼為依住三摩地；若退彼相，便不能住。
items.en: One who thus cultivates the light-concentration meets eleven kinds of concentration-difficulty — doubt and the rest, as the scripture explains at length. Question: whose difficulties are these? Answer: the marks of concentration. The marks are of two kinds: the object-mark and the causal mark. Resting on these, one abides in concentration; if one loses those marks, one cannot abide.

items.title: The Eleven Difficulties, One by One

items.zh: 此中最初，於所顯現光明色相不善知故，便覺有疑。方便緩故，有不作意。如於眾色不欲見者，或閉於目，或復背面；此觀行者，於諸色中不欲作意，亦復如是。由不善守根門等故，有身麁重。多習睡眠，或多覺悟，便增惛睡，不見眾色；設有所見而不圓滿。為此二事，極作功用力勵思惟，故有太過勇猛精進。
items.en: Here the first: because one does not well know the light-and-form mark that appears, doubt arises. Because the effort is slack, there is non-attention. As one who does not want to see forms shuts his eyes or turns his back, so this contemplative, not wanting to attend to forms, is likewise [obstructed]. Because one does not well guard the sense-doors and the rest, there is bodily heaviness. Sleeping too much, or waking too much, dullness-and-sleep increases, so one does not see forms, or, seeing them, sees incompletely. Straining effort against these two, there is excessive exertion.

items.zh: 由有太過策勵過故，還極下劣。如急捉持斥鷃鳥者。彼唯思求光明之相，此與見色若俱生時，悕一得二，便生踊躍；猶如有人得二伏藏。遍於諸方，欻然並見不祥之色，便生大怖；猶如有人兩邊旋轉卒起。彼於行時，或復住時、於世雜類起種種想；如是外想，與定為難。或復因其所修習定，謂己為勝，觀他為劣，便自高舉。如是亦得名種種想。
items.en: Because of that excessive spurring, one sinks back into extreme sluggishness — like one who grips a quail too tightly. Seeking only the mark of light, when it arises together with the seeing of form — hoping for one and getting two — one leaps with elation, like a man who finds two buried treasures. Seeing, all at once, inauspicious forms in every direction, one is seized with great fear, like a man startled by something spinning up on both sides. Whether moving or resting, one gives rise to assorted thoughts of the world's medley — such external thoughts are a difficulty for concentration. Or, on account of the concentration cultivated, one thinks oneself superior and regards others as inferior, and grows self-exalted — this too is called an assorted thought.

items.title: The Last Two Difficulties, and How They Undo a Concentration

items.zh: 或多言論，或久尋思，令身疲勞，心不得定；如是多言，與定為難。若從定生光明之相，及見色時，便捨內修相續作意，願樂於外諦視眾色；故極思察，與定為難。如是諸難，隨其所應，障三摩地所緣境相及因緣相。或有遇此，退失所緣、因緣相故，如其次第，二相俱沒。
items.en: Or, by much talk or prolonged pondering, the body is wearied and the mind cannot settle — such much-talking is a difficulty for concentration. If, when light arises from the concentration and forms are seen, one abandons the continuous inner cultivation and, delighting in the outward, stares intently at the forms — this over-scrutiny is a difficulty for concentration. All such difficulties, each as fits, obstruct the object-mark and the causal mark of concentration; and some, meeting them, lose the object-mark and the causal mark, so that in sequence both marks sink away.

items.title: Concentration by Its Feeling, and the Four Aims of Cultivating Concentration

items.zh: 復次，云何喜俱行三摩地？謂初二靜慮諸三摩地。云何樂俱行三摩地？謂第三靜慮諸三摩地。云何捨俱行三摩地？謂第四靜慮已上諸三摩地。復次，云何修定為得現法樂住？謂於四種現法樂住方便道中所有修定，及未圓滿清淨鮮白諸根本地所有修定。為顯修習未曾得定，是故世尊說初靜慮前方便道。云何修定為得智見？謂諸苾芻，於光明相，慇懃懇到審諦而取，如經廣說。當知此在能發天眼前方便道所有修定。此中天眼，於諸色境能照、能觀，說名為見。能知諸天如是名字、如是種類，乃至廣說，如勝天經，是名為智。
items.en: Furthermore, what is concentration accompanied by joy? The concentrations of the first and second dhyānas. Accompanied by bliss? The concentrations of the third dhyāna. Accompanied by equanimity? The concentrations of the fourth dhyāna and above. Furthermore, what is cultivating concentration for a pleasant abiding in this very life? The cultivation of concentration on the preparatory path towards the four pleasant abidings of this life, and the cultivation of concentration in the root grounds not yet perfectly pure and bright. What is cultivating concentration for knowledge-and-vision? Monks who, upon the mark of light, take it up earnestly, thoroughly, and rightly, as the scripture explains at length. Know that this is the cultivation of concentration on the preparatory path that can generate the divine eye. Here the divine eye, illumining and contemplating form-objects, is called "vision"; knowing the gods' such names, such kinds, and so on at length — as in the Supreme-Gods Sūtra — is called "knowledge."

items.zh: 云何修定生分別慧？謂諦現觀預流果向方便道中所有修定，或為修習諸無礙解。云何修定為盡諸漏？謂阿羅漢果方便道中所有修定。
items.en: What is cultivating concentration for giving rise to discerning wisdom? The cultivation of concentration on the preparatory path of the direct realisation of the truths, towards the fruit of stream-entry; or for cultivating the analytic knowledges. What is cultivating concentration for exhausting the outflows? The cultivation of concentration on the preparatory path towards the fruit of arhatship.

items.zh: 復次，云何五聖智三摩地？
items.en: Further, what is the concentration of the five noble knowledges?

blocks.text: Today's reading contains a practical list every meditator can use: eleven difficulties that disrupt concentration, illustrated by our teachers with memorable stories. It closes with four aims for which concentration is cultivated.

subs.head: Where the immeasurables reach their height

blocks.text: Each immeasurable reaches its height at a particular level of absorption, and only noble ones truly cultivate them as path factors.

In the light-concentration, one may attend only to light or only to forms (partial cultivation), or to both, discerning light and seeing forms within it (complete). The divine eye develops from the complete form.
The light-concentration meets eleven difficulties. Master Cháng Bǎi, following the *Pīxún jì*: four obstruct reflection-wisdom, seven obstruct cultivation-wisdom. Among them:

items: **Non-attention**, "like one who shuts his eyes or turns away". Both teachers tell the story of the old woman east of the city who would not look at the Buddha: when he came from the east she turned west; from above, she looked down; even covering her face, she saw him through her fingers. Turning away from what is good for us is a real obstacle.

**Excessive effort**, "like gripping a quail too tightly". Master Cháng Bǎi: grip a bird too hard and it escapes; "too urgent and body and mind are exhausted; too slack and one cannot grasp the mark".
**Much talk**, which wearies the body. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Never mind ordinary talk; even explaining the Dharma, if you talk too much it drains your energy."

blocks.text: The list is almost a portrait of a meditation retreat: doubt on the first day, then dullness, then forcing it, then talking too much, then clinging to a good sit.
Concentrations accompanied by joy belong to the first and second dhyānas; by bliss, the third; by equanimity, the fourth and above.
Concentration is cultivated for four aims:

items: **happiness here and now**: the four dhyānas, each with its preparatory "threshold" concentration (Venerable Miào Jìng);
**knowledge and vision**: the divine eye; "vision" is seeing forms, "knowledge" is knowing the gods' names and kinds;
**discerning wisdom**: on the path towards stream-entry. Venerable Miào Jìng: the fifteen moments of the path of seeing are the cause; the sixteenth is the fruit;

blocks.text: Only the last two lead out of saṃsāra. The first two are valuable but, like the wheel-turning king's pleasures (Day 29), remain within it.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how do partial and complete cultivation of concentration differ?
options: partial attends only to light or only to forms; complete attends to both, discerning light and seeing forms
quiz.why: "Either attending only to the mark of light or attending only to the mark of form, one enters the concentration … Attending to both, one enters the concentration, discerning light and also seeing forms." Master Cháng Bǎi: the *Madhyama Āgama* presents this as a method for the divine eye.

quiz.q: "Non-attention" is likened to one who shuts his eyes or turns away. What story do the teachers tell?
options: the old woman east of the city — when the Buddha came from the east she turned west, from above she looked down, and even with eyes shut she still saw him
the blind men and the elephant
covering ears to steal a bell
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "When the Buddha came from the east, she turned her head west; from above, she bowed her head" (*Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra*, fascicle 9). Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Buddha showed her many forms; she shut her eyes — I won't look! — yet with eyes closed she still saw."

quiz.q: Excessive effort leads to sluggishness, "like gripping a quail too tightly." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the simile?
options: like catching a bird — grip too hard and it escapes; too urgent exhausts body and mind, too slack fails to grasp the mark
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Like catching a bird — grip too hard and it flies off. Meditation too: too urgent and body and mind are exhausted; too slow and one can't grasp the mark." Venerable Miào Jìng: gripping too hard tires you and can't be sustained. The reading note's "crushing the bird" isn't in the lecture.

quiz.q: "Much talk" wearies the body. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say about talking even about the Dharma?
options: even explaining the Dharma, talking too much drains one's energy
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Never mind ordinary talk — even explaining the Dharma, if you talk too much it drains your energy." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Prolonged pondering hurts the spirit, tiring body and mind, scattering the mind so it can't settle."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which dhyānas are the joy-, bliss-, and equanimity-accompanied concentrations?
options: joy — first and second dhyānas; bliss — the third; equanimity — the fourth and above
quiz.why: "The concentrations of the first and second dhyānas" are joy-accompanied; "of the third dhyāna," bliss-accompanied; "of the fourth dhyāna and above," equanimity-accompanied. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four formless attainments all go with equanimity.

quiz.q: In "cultivating concentration for knowledge and vision," what are vision and knowledge?
options: the divine eye illumining and contemplating forms is "vision"; knowing gods' names and kinds is "knowledge" — the preparatory path to the divine eye
quiz.why: "Here the divine eye, illumining and contemplating form-objects, is called 'vision'; knowing the gods' such names, such kinds, and so on … is called 'knowledge.'" Venerable Miào Jìng, citing Kuiji: not only gods but every realm.

quiz.q: "Concentration for discerning wisdom" is on the path towards stream-entry. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish the candidate from the fruit?
options: fifteen moments are the candidacy, the cause; the sixteenth moment is the fruit of stream-entry
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "These fifteen moments are called the candidacy for stream-entry, its cause; at the sixteenth moment it's the fruit." The text: concentration "on the preparatory path of the direct realisation of the truths, towards the fruit of stream-entry."
